rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration with standard encoders (scgpt for RNA, imagenet_vit_l for images) and key components (transformer aggregation, concat fusion) to establish performance. This isolates the effect of multimodal integration and multiprofile settings, which are critical design choices. It balances exploration by testing a complex yet reasonable configuration without overcomplicating with unnecessary changes.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves 0.507 validation accuracy. This experiment tests replacing transformer aggregation with avgpool while keeping other components identical, isolating the impact of aggregation method. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether aggregation strategy significantly affects performance, a critical design choice with minimal prior evidence. This comparison is more informative than testing rna_only or other multi-variant changes, and aligns with principles of focused exploration.

Existing evidence shows avgpool aggregation (config_009) outperforms transformer (config_001). This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion (while keeping other parameters identical) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion method. It directly addresses uncertainty about fusion's impact, aligns with balancing exploration and exploitation, and avoids unnecessary parameter changes.

Existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion improve performance (config_016: 0.542 accuracy). This experiment tests whether changing the RNA encoder from scgpt to scvi_n200 further improves performance while keeping the effective aggregation/fusion strategy, isolating the impact of representation choice.

Existing evidence shows config_011 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other components identical. It isolates the effect of aggregation method on performance, a critical design choice with potential for improvement. This balances exploitation of the strong scvi_n200/resnet50 foundation with exploration of aggregation methods.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder with weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (config_017: 0.713). This experiment tests the effect of aggregation method by comparing transformer (config_017) vs None (config_007), isolating the impact of aggregation on performance. It addresses uncertainty about whether transformer aggregation is critical for success, balancing exploitation of promising components with exploration of design choices.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (config_017: 0.713). This experiment tests whether multiprofile setting (vs singleprofile) can match this performance when using the same RNA/image encoders but switching aggregation from transformer to avgpool. This isolates the impact of profile setting and aggregation, both critical factors with sparse evidence in multiprofile scenarios.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_017) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation while maintaining the same RNA/image encoders and weighted fusion clarifies the impact of aggregation method on performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation while preserving other high-performing components, balancing exploitation of known strengths with exploration of design choices.

Existing evidence shows that models using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and transformer aggregation (e.g., config_017) achieve high performance. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (while keeping other parameters identical) impacts accuracy, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It directly compares a key design choice with strong prior evidence, balancing exploitation of promising directions and exploration of critical components.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_017) achieves high accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether changing the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l while keeping other parameters the same (scvi_n200 RNA, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) affects performance. This isolates the impact of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision with uncertain optimal value.
